newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN HOTEL INDUSTRY WARNS GOVT OF TAX CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN HOTEL INDUSTRY WARNS GOVT OF TAX CRISIS.

text.p: Australian alcohol and tobacco industry representatives on Friday warned Treasury officials of a looming crisis because of changes to taxes affecting their businesses.
Australian Hotels Association respresentatives told reporters they had warned officials that the changes meant the alcohol industry was being taxed twice -- by both the state and federal governments.

"They weren't able to deliver us satisfaction but they certainly understood what we were talking about and they made it clear that the government doesn't want any form of double taxation," Australian Hotels Association vice president Peter Hurley told reporters after meeting with officials.

On Wednesday, Treasurer Peter Costello announced that the federal government would replace petrol, alcohol and tobacco franchise fees levied by the state governments with a new regime of uniform national taxes.
Under the new system, wholesale tax on alcohol increased by 15 percent, while customs and excise duty on petrol increased by 8.1 cents a litre and on tobacco by A$167 a kg.
However, in some states, retailers had already pre-paid state taxes and Hurley said the states were now refusing to refund the advance fees.

"No states or territories have indicated yet that they will refund the pre-paid component because they are claiming that it would constitute a windfall gain and therefore only involve a 100 percent tax anyway," Hurley said.
"We argue that that's not the case because it's not a windfall gain."
He said alcohol prices would certainly rise if the advance fees were not refunded.
The tax revamp was forced by the High Court's majority decision released on Tuesday that the state taxes were unconstitutional as only the federal government could levy such taxes.
